data.title: 1 in 4 Ebola deaths are children in Democratic Republic of Congo's worst outbreak
data.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo is battling its deadliest outbreak of Ebola, caused by a rare strain with no approved treatment. With children losing parents, facing an estimated 60 per cent fatality rate and making up more than a quarter of deaths, experts say children are taking the brunt of the disease.

data.title: Is sisterhood the secret to a long life? The Sardinian village that could hold key to women’s longevity
data.description: Meet some of the elderly residents of Bolotana, in line to be the world’s sixth ‘blue zone’ for its high number of female centenarians When Giovanna Marras opens the door to her home in Bolotana, a mountain village in central Sardinia, her eyes are bright with curiosity as she sizes up her visitors. Her sister, Mariangela, peeks out too, soon ushering her guests inside and handing out dishes of ice-cream. The sisters are full of life, talking animatedly. Giovanna is 101 and Mariangela is 99. Sitting in their living room, Giovanna swiftly recaps her life story: she excelled at school before moving to Cagliari, the capital of the Italian island, at 18 to train as a seamstress. The sisters went on to run a successful tailoring business in Bolotana before travelling the world after retirement. Neither married. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘4,000 people minding our own business’: four decades on, Falklands again face a hostile Argentina
data.description: Facing a slump in the polls, Argentina’s president is making economic attacks on the islands’ oil industry, and suggesting its key fisheries industry could be next A dozen local people and a uniformed military police officer (“Do you mind if I sit in?”) took their seats at the back of the handsome wood-panelled courtroom that doubles as the Falkland Islands’ legislative assembly. Outside, it was a typically blowy early evening. It may nominally be spring in the south Atlantic, but Stanley harbour, with its dark grey water speckled with historical shipwrecks, was a cauldron of swells and churn. Six of the assembly’s eight members – five men, one woman – waited patiently at a row of desks and microphones. The heating had been turned up to just short of uncomfortable. Behind them, a portrait of King Charles. From the other walls, dusty photographs of governors, of varying popularity, gazed disinterestedly at the scene. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘How do we welcome the stranger, with humanity or anger?’ The forgotten Germans who found refuge in Ireland
data.description: A new play revisits the story of Ireland’s 18th-century German refugees, whose experience of prejudice and exclusion resonates with today’s debates over immigration In the early 18th century, a few thousand Germans fled religious persecution and near starvation in their homeland and ended up in remote rural Irish villages. The Irish Palatines, as they were known, were poor, conservative homesteaders who couldn’t speak the language and were the object of suspicion and violence – precursors to the displaced Syrians or Afghans of the past decade. Their story is told in Refuge, a co-production between Staatstheater Mainz and the Irish company Fishamble. Part love story, part social commentary, it is performed by a mixed cast, mainly in English but with some German interludes. Continue reading...

data.title: Going nowhere fast? Personal trainers on why you aren’t seeing results in the gym
data.description: From doing too much cardio to wasting time – PTs reveal the common fails stunting your progress, and how to avoid them We’ve all done it. Launched ourselves head first into a new regime – perhaps as the result of a new year resolution, recent breakup or aggressively unflattering photo. “You go all in and train five days a week,” says Elizabeth Davies, personal trainer and author of Training for Your Old Lady Body . “Then life happens. You miss a few sessions, then stop completely. You feel deflated that you couldn’t stick to it. Then some time later, motivation strikes again and the cycle repeats itself.” Continue reading...

data.title: ‘We hang on to summer a little longer here’: five of the best places for autumn sun in Europe and Turkey
data.description: If you’re looking for a last blast of summer, these sunny resorts offer quiet beaches but enough life to stave off the end-of-season blues A Kalkan sunset is always a beautiful thing – the horseshoe-shaped bay deepening to azure blue against an apricot-rose sky – but, in October, when the light is low and the sun drops early, it’s almost transcendentally lovely. In some Turkish resorts, you’d be sitting watching it surrounded by quiet streets, half-empty bars and that melancholic sense that another season is over. In Kalkan, it still feels like summer; the harbourfront restaurants throng with visitors, the day gulets (wooden boats) still putter in and out of the bay and you don’t have to wait an hour to get a taxi back to your villa. Continue reading...

data.title: Intensifying drone attacks on ships in Black Sea bring war ever closer to Nato shores
data.description: Six attacks in 10 days by suspected Russian drones mark dramatic escalation in maritime conflict The first the crew of the Bulgarian ferry Dioscuria knew of an attack on a cargo ship in their country’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea in the early hours of 6 October was a distant explosion 70 miles off the coastal town of Byala. The Turkish-owned Alfa Watan, heading for the Romanian port of Sulina, had been struck by suspected Russian air and naval drones. Arriving on the scene, Dioscuria found an overturned lifeboat and lifejackets in the water. There was no sign, however, of Alfa Watan’s crew of 10. Continue reading...

data.title: US corporate lobbyists mounted ‘blitz’ to dilute landmark EU deforestation law, report finds
data.description: Environmental watchdog Mighty Earth reveals two-year effort to postpone and weaken EU Deforestation Regulation US corporate lobbyists launched a two-year “blitz” to postpone and weaken the world’s most progressive legislation to protect forests, according to a new investigation by the environmental watchdog Mighty Earth. Major US firms and trade associations, including Cargill, Bunge, Mondelēz and the US Soybean Export Council, as well as numerous other US firms and organizations, sought to influence the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) in more than 350 meetings, the advocacy group found . Continue reading...

data.title: Attacked from the sky: Sudanese goldminers count deadly cost of eking out a living on the Egypt border
data.description: As civil war has left their country in ruins, many young Sudanese have turned to artisanal mining. An airstrike on a mine last week killed more than 100 and has provoked anger against Egypt, seen as the most likely suspect Torches still fixed on their heads but tools cast aside, the Sudanese goldminers of the North Valley had already mounted an impromptu rescue operation by the time Ammar* arrived at the site of a suspected Egyptian airstrike. At least 114 were killed, according to the Sudanese rights group Emergency Lawyers, in the strike on Saturday 10 October on an artisanal goldmine brimming with young Sudanese trying to eke out a living in a country where the economy has been shattered by three years of war. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘A key artist in her own right’: wallpaper and fabrics designer emerges from William Morris’s shadow
data.description: Creativity and influence of Morris & Co designer Kate Faulkner to be detailed in Cambridge exhibition For more than a century, she has been little more than a footnote in William Morris’s story, her work mistaken for his, her contribution to British decorative art largely overlooked. Yet, in her lifetime, Kate Faulkner was a pioneer: the first person after Morris to design wallpapers and fabrics for Morris & Co, and one of only four designers he ever trusted to do so. Several of the patterns she designed under her name for the company in the 1870s and 1880s are still sold today. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It was like your worst nightmare’ – Ellie and Natasia on mums, music … and failing to make Bob Mortimer smile
data.description: They spoofed mothers … and now they are mothers. The comedians talk about moving with the times for the return of their scalpel-sharp BBC sketch show Before Ellie White and Natasia Demetriou were mothers, they were mums. In a skit from their 2019 sketch show pilot, the comedy duo play two straight-talking, hygiene-obsessed matriarchs in gilets and camel-toe-accentuating leggings who record lifestyle vlogs from a pristine kitchen while melodramatically referencing the pressures of motherhood. Ever since, the characters have become a core component of the pair’s comic universe, appearing repeatedly in the first proper series of Ellie & Natasia in 2022 . Now the mums are back and moving with the times: reviewing various supermarket white breads – all reassuringly “sterile” options – as car-based food influencers for the show’s second outing. But behind the scenes there has been a bigger shift. The last time they wrote these sketches, White and Demetriou were childless; now they each have two kids. Continue reading...

data.title: My longterm boyfriend died last year. Is it too soon to date someone new? | Ask Annalisa Barbieri
data.description: Only you can know when you are ready, but a year is not long to process grief, and you seem to have doubts about this man My long term boyfriend died of cancer last year. We’d been together for 16 years , since I was 21 and he was 23. I had given birth to our only child three weeks before his diagnosis. My son was just shy of 10 months old when his dad died, and he’s now turned two. I loved my late partner deeply and had planned to stay with him for ever. We were embarking on an 18-year project together, raising our son. Now I think, how can I ever be happy again ? Continue reading...

data.title: Blunder in, abandon allies and court a dictator: it’s the Trump doctrine, now playing out in Myanmar | Steve Bloomfield
data.description: The US condemned the genocide and military rule there, but now that Trump craves its rare earths, that’s all changed. For democracy activists, that’s a disaster Marco Rubio was once adamant that the US had to do everything in its power to end what he described as the “ethnic cleansing” of the Rohingya in Myanmar. In a 2017 letter he signed along with 20 other US senators , Rubio called for “strong multilateral sanctions against specific senior Burmese military officials associated with the gross human rights abuses”. Those responsible for the atrocities should be prosecuted, he argued. In the years since, the Myanmar military’s crimes have only increased. What was then deemed ethnic cleansing of the Rohingya is now widely viewed, including by the US, as genocide. What little democracy existed in Myanmar was eradicated in 2021 when Aung San Suu Kyi was arrested and imprisoned and her party’s election victory overturned, and the military took full control. Continue reading...

data.title: Finally, everyone fancies James Acaster. What took them so long? | Polly Hudson
data.description: His good-natured camaraderie on The Traitors has turned him into a viral heartthrob. What these Johnny Come Latelys don’t realise is that he’s always been a man for our times It’s hard not to wonder how James Acaster feels at the moment. On the one hand, everybody suddenly fancies him, which must be flattering. On the other, all the language around the phenomenon is stuff like “unlikely”, “unexpected” and “bizarre crush”, which is presumably … less so. But there’s no denying that he is now a viral heartthrob, which sounds like something that requires urgent medical attention, but isn’t. After each episode of The Celebrity Traitors, social media is flooded with slow-motion edits and thirst-trap clips of Acaster, including one of him in the castle set to Ginuwine’s Pony that has received more than 500,000 views and counting. Vogue declared that his “specifically east London-y wardrobe has captured the hearts and minds of millennial women countrywide”, and anointed him its “new internet boyfriend”. For longtime Acaster admirers, loyal listeners to the Off Menu podcast who rooted for him on the seventh series of Taskmaster, this is bittersweet. The smug plus side: we were right all along. The lemony minus: now we have to share him. It’s like those people who saw Oasis in a tiny working-man’s club when they didn’t have a record deal. I fancied Acaster long before this crowd of Johnny Come Latelys at the BBC TV equivalent of Knebworth. Continue reading...

data.title: The hill I will die on: Cinemas have been getting away with lies. Films should begin on time | Jeffrey Ingold
data.description: If cinemas must run 20 minutes of adverts before a feature, they could at least be honest about it. Or, I have a better solution … Do you remember the last time you were lied to? I certainly do. I was tricked by the North Finchley Vue, which sold me and my boyfriend tickets to a 7.15pm showing of The Odyssey. Guess what was playing at 7.15pm? A car advert. Ten minutes later, it was a trailer for the horror film Werwulf. Then there was an advert for Vue – as if I wasn’t already there. The film was half an hour late to its own showing when it finally started at 7.45pm. I am sick and tired of cinemas getting away with such treachery. I don’t want to follow in the footsteps of my friend, who knows that the ads at her local run for 22 minutes so slinks in at just the right time. I shouldn’t have to do mental maths because I am being lied to by cinemas. We are all the victims of their predatory time-wasting system. Jeffrey Ingold is a freelance journalist covering LGBTQ+ issues, music and culture Continue reading...

data.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
data.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

data.title: Daniel Dubois delivers devastating second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley to retain WBO title
data.description: Dubois underlines status as Britain’s leading heavyweight Wardley’s corner throw in the towel in second round Daniel Dubois overwhelmed Fabio Wardley in their WBO world title fight on Saturday night as he continued his quest to become the most authoritative heavyweight fighter on the planet with this crushing victory. This was the second time in five months that Dubois has defeated Wardley but, after their fight of the year contender in May , he unleashed a shockingly one-sided shellacking. After two minutes and 21 seconds of round two, Wardley was rescued from the bludgeoning fists of Dubois by the referee, just as the fluttering white towel of his trainer, Ben Davison, sailed over the ropes in surrender. Davison had been on the brink of throwing in the towel at the very end of the opening round but the bell sounded to end a disastrous first three minutes for Wardley. He was dropped heavily after just 17 seconds as Dubois landed a left cross followed by a pulverising right hand. Continue reading...

The whole stadium observed a minute’s silence while Andrews’s No 5 shirt was laid on the pitch before kick-off. La Rochelle’s three South African players presented a jersey to their visitors in memory of the player, who died on Friday at Lions’ hotel on the nearby Ile de Ré. data.title: Kartal battles past Ostapenko in Wuhan to secure spot in first WTA 1000 final
data.description: The 24-year-old becomes new British No 1 Biggest final of career after six months out with injury Sonay Kartal’s dream comeback continues as the Briton beat Jelena Ostapenko in straight sets on Saturday to advance to the biggest final of her career at the Wuhan Open. Kartal was behind in both sets and fought off six set points to claim a 7-6 (9), 7-6 (5) win over the former French Open champion in her second tour-level tournament back after injury. The 24-year-old, who started this week ranked world No 170 due to her recent inactivity, becomes the lowest-ranked player to reach a WTA 1000 final since the format began in 2009. The victory means Kartal is guaranteed to jump into the world’s top 50 in the WTA rankings next week, overtaking Katie Boulter to become the British No 1. Continue reading...

data.title: Inside the long, bitter fight over one man’s quest to build the biggest AI datacenter in California
data.description: A modern-day prospector promised rural Imperial thousands of jobs and millions in tax revenue – but his plan has set off a firestorm of resistance Sebastian Rucci zoomed in on a map in late 2024, looking closely at a large block of brown earth. The barren plot sandwiched between sprawling alfalfa fields and sleepy desert suburbs was exactly what he’d been searching for – the perfect place to realize his dream of building the largest artificial intelligence datacenter in California. The dusty expanse wasn’t an obvious location. It was in the Sonoran desert, just north of the Mexican border, where temperatures regularly rose past 100F (37.8C). Water was scarce in the once-booming agricultural area, which gets its supply from the beleaguered Colorado River. And then, there was the city of Imperial – population 22,000 – to win over. As controversial datacenter projects have sprung up across the US, residents were naturally skeptical of a new, energy-guzzling neighbor. Continue reading...

data.title: Honeybees are barging aside wild pollinators in hunt for pollen and nectar, study finds
data.description: As a surge in beekeepers has led to increased numbers of honeybees, researchers record them pushing bumblebees and other rival species away from flowers Honeybees are outcompeting wild pollinators for resources by aggressively bumping into them and chasing them away from flowers, research has shown. The study , by researchers from Anglia Ruskin University, found that areas where there were higher concentrations of honeybees had fewer wild pollinators, such as bumblebees, solitary bees and hoverflies. data.title: Heat pumps and insulation would cut UK living costs more than new oilfields, study suggests
data.description: Warm homes plan would create 50,000 jobs, compared with about 1,100 for Rosebank oilfield, thinktank finds Insulating Britain’s homes and investing in heat pumps would do more to cut the cost of living, create jobs and boost the UK’s economy than drilling for new oil, research suggests. The government’s £15bn warm homes plan, currently under threat of cuts as ministers seek budget savings , would slash £1bn a year from household energy bills across the UK, concentrated on those on low incomes, according to research by the thinktank E3G. It would also provide a £1.6bn yearly boost to the economy, and about 50,000 new jobs spread across thousands of small businesses. Continue reading...

data.title: Stinky business: south London bike shop hit by ‘unbearable’ stench from Thames Water sewer
data.description: Owner and mechanics fear for their health and future of the Herne Hill shop with no date for fixing problem The leafy south London neighbourhood of Herne Hill is a haven for cyclists who can often be seen lapping the local parks and refuelling at the many cafes that line the suburban streets. But there is something foul in the air of this corner of the capital – and for once it’s not the traffic fumes hitting bicycle riders. A toxic stench thought to be caused by untreated sewage stuck in Thames Water drains has been emanating from the subterranean depths for months, most likely caused by the summer’s lack of rain. data.title: UAE agrees with Saudi Arabia to re-enter Yemen conflict amid Houthi gains
data.description: United Arab Emirates will reportedly resume payments to Yemeni forces as gains by Iran-backed Houthi fighters alarm Gulf state rulers Yemen civil war: what sparked latest escalation and who is involved? The United Arab Emirates has agreed to re-enter the Yemen conflict by resuming payments to some government forces fighting Iran-aligned Houthis in the south, according to sources in Yemen. In return, Saudi Arabia has agreed to provide air cover for the anti-Houthi force. The new cooperation agreement is the first tangible sign that the deep rift between the UAE and Saudi Arabia over Yemen’s future is starting to be healed – if only because the advance by Houthi forces across Yemen has alarmed all the rival Gulf state rulers. data.title: ‘I drunkenly sing Wonderwall off-key and awfully’: Rebecca Ferguson’s honest playlist
data.description: The singer-songwriter gets a lift from U2 and likes to reminisce to Bette Midler, but which cheesy Euro banger does she secretly like? The first song I fell in love with When I was five or six, my mum wouldn’t let me listen to anything other than Christian gospel. Her friend Jane felt sorry for me and brought me a cassette with Whitney Houston on one side and Cher on the other. My ears couldn’t believe what they were hearing. I Will Always Love You made me think: This is what I’m going to do. The first single I bought So Young by the Corrs, from Sainsbury’s in Walton Village in Liverpool. I couldn’t really afford music as a kid, so buying a record was a big deal. I’d heard the Corrs on the radio, liked their voices and thought: I’m buying this. Continue reading...

data.title: Poldark’s resilience helped me turn round my business
data.description: Staffing issues, financial woes, equipment failure and a thousand other things made it seem as if being the boss of a dental practice wasn’t for me, but TV’s burly hero inspired me to push on I discovered the TV series Poldark about a year into a new business, an ill-fitting professional identity, and life in a new city. Having worked for others since dental school, I’d taken possession of a practice the year I turned 30. The practice needed serious refurbishment. I bought it despite dire warnings that my plans for the building, and the way I wanted to treat patients, couldn’t keep a practice in the black. After months of frigid rooms (the building barely had central heating) and frantic clinics, being constantly reminded I hadn’t yet accrued years of trust like the previous owner, I found myself in the upstairs office at 8pm on a Monday, weeping over a spreadsheet. data.title: Charlie Vickers: ‘Tom Cruise cheated at freediving – that’s the headline’
data.description: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power star on his muddy marriage proposal, controversial cheese opinions, memories of Sam Neill and having a good evil face You once played Basil Fawlty in an amateur student production of Fawlty Towers at Queen’s College in Melbourne. How amateur was your Basil Fawlty moustache? It was terrible. It was real but it was definitely coloured in – I still have holes in my beard. I’d also shaved my head, so if you look at the early promo posters, you can clearly see I’m wearing a wig. Our theatre was closed so we had to perform in a circus tent in the middle of winter, on an oval in the university grounds, which was all very Fawlty Towers. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Sometimes it’s not perfect, but it works’: film-maker Charles Burnett on his chronicling of Black working-class life
data.description: A restored version of his 1983 film My Brother’s Wedding, set in South Central LA, brings Burnett’s vision to a new audience Charles Burnett had a dilemma. He had agreed to attend the wedding of a co-worker, but the wedding was scheduled for the same day and time as a funeral for a childhood friend. Initially, the film-maker – a landmark chronicler of Black working-class lives – decided he’d go to the funeral. But when he tried to break the news to the co-worker, she was so dejected that he couldn’t go through with it. He tried asking the bride to change the wedding – which was “ridiculous to think of trying to do”, he says decades later – but that didn’t work either. He decided he’d go to both events. data.title: Buvette, London WC2: ‘It’s actually rather lovely’ – restaurant review | Grace Dent on restaurants
data.description: This offshoot of a New York favourite isn’t reinventing the wheel, but it does bring a touch of Gallic glam to the neighbourhood A faux-French, cult-hit New York brasserie has opened in Neal’s Yard, deep in the hairy armpit of Covent Garden among alleyways where holistic therapy rooms, walk-in back rub spaces, Neal’s Yard Remedies and 26 Grains cafe are its immediate neighbours. The windchimes and the whiff of patchouli part the air round these parts, and the footfall is yoga pant-clad and hungry for hummus. Buvette , meanwhile, has brought a touch of Gallic glam to the neighbourhood, and is clearly aimed at the Emily in Paris generation with its totalement français menu featuring croque monsieur with roast mushrooms and gruyere, rillettes de saumon or salade niçoise with haricots verts and a mollet egg; there’s also a Macvin champagne and muscadet spritz, pastis on the rocks, warm scones with jam, and almond croissants. This is the London arm of Jody Williams’ West Village gastrothèque , and its menu is a pretty card listing 25 dishes to choose from, none of them above £18. It clearly thinks it’s a hot, fresh, new thing, but I’m not sure it’s anything new at all. We used to call places that looked like this Café Rouge : that is, recognisably French, and by that I mean recognisable if you have a working GCSE knowledge of La Rochelle cafe life. It’s that version of French dining that won’t scare the horses, or at least the horses that the French haven’t minced coarsely and served in their own gastroduodenal canals with an exemplary homemade moutarde . Continue reading...

data.title: Alexandra Shulman: ‘Which book am I ashamed not to have read? Literally the whole canon of classic English literature’
data.description: The former British Vogue editor-in-chief and author on a romantic kiss on a traffic island, her school-run regrets, and a very expensive nude Born in London, Alexandra Shulman, 68, studied social anthropology at the University of Sussex. She was a secretary at Over 21 magazine and, in the early 80s, became a journalist at Tatler. In 1990, she was made editor of British GQ and, from 1992 to 2017, she was editor‑in‑chief of British Vogue. For her contribution to fashion journalism, she was awarded both an OBE and a CBE. Her books include novels and the bestselling memoir, Clothes … and Other Things That Matter. A collection of essays, Black Coffee and Red Lipstick: Notes on Living , is out now. She is married for the second time, has a son and lives in London. When were you happiest? Anytime that I’m lying in the sun next to a swimming pool with a good book. Continue reading...

data.title: Fake Linda and me: the Agatha Christie-worthy mystery of the fraudster who stole my byline
data.description: How a string of bizarre events led writer Linda Geddes to don her sleuthing cap and dig into a world of shadowy impersonators It started with an entirely ordinary interaction on LinkedIn. Someone had tagged me in a post, saying how much they’d enjoyed contributing to a New York Post article I’d written about “chronoworking”. As the author of a book about circadian rhythms, it was exactly the sort of subject I might write about. Except I’d never heard of this person, let alone interviewed them. I clicked on the link and my stomach dropped. There, above an article about people who organise their working lives around their biological clocks, was my name: Linda Geddes. Continue reading...

data.title: Hiding in plane sight: the invisible turbulence that can strike out of a clear blue sky
data.description: As the planet warms, airlines are grappling with what this means for air travel – and for the passengers who simply refuse to keep their seatbelts fastened It was a swelteringly hot afternoon in south-west Myanmar on 21 May 2024. Tropical thunderstorms, showers and highs of 36C were forecast for the area around the Irrawaddy Basin. High above, monsoonal heat and humidity were building into a vast convective column of water vapour, a towering cumulonimbus cloud soaring up to 35,000ft (more than 10,500 metres) into the air. From the ground, it would have looked like something from a children’s picture book – a soft, fluffy white mass. But for Singapore Airlines flight SQ321 passing just above, it was anything but benign. In the cabin of the Boeing 777, passengers were being woken up for breakfast with three hours to go on the journey from London to Singapore. For the 210 travellers on board, the past 10 hours had been uneventful. The seatbelt signs were off. Some were milling around, others were using the toilets, and cabin staff were preparing trolleys for service. At 2.19pm and 23 seconds local time, moderate turbulence shook the plane for 17 seconds and the seatbelt sign was switched on. Then, as one passenger described it, it was “like a grenade had gone off”. In just 4.6 seconds, any passenger not strapped in hit the roof with 1.5 times the force of gravity and was thrown back on the floor in an instant. Continue reading...

data.title: The last lace mill – in pictures
data.description: MYB Textiles Ltd is the last mill in the world weaving patterned Nottingham lace on traditional looms. Once there were 20 lace mills in the Irvine Valley towns of Newmilns and Darvel alone. The lace industry became the largest employer in the area for a time and flourished until the late 1970s when competition emerged from other European countries and Asia. Now the majority of their trade comes from the film, theatre, TV and entertainment industry Continue reading...

data.title: Buildings set ablaze and more than 1,200 arrested as police clash with protesters across France
data.description: Police fire teargas in Paris and Limoges town hall ‘largely lost’ to fire – with officials blaming violence on ‘ultra-left’ More than 1,200 people were arrested in France on Saturday after protesters supporting high school students clashed with police, with some demonstrations later spiralling out of control as buildings were set ablaze and shops looted. Police fired teargas in confrontations with protesters, as demonstrations across France were boosted by other groups angry about high prices and the fraying of a social welfare system. While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully in street marches in scores of cities, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, luxury boutiques and supermarkets and attacked police vehicles and officers. Continue reading...

data.title: Ukraine war briefing: Trump’s sanctions waiver is a ‘60-day pause’ to analyse economic impact, says Rubio
data.description: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy expects Trump to lift more sanctions against Russia. What we know on day 1,698 US secretary of state Marco Rubio has said that US President Donald Trump’s waiver of sweeping sanctions and tariffs on Russia would be a 60-day pause to “analyse” their impact on the global economy. Rubio said also no one at the White House ordered the slow down of the speed of Ukraine’s access to Starlink to prevent it from being used on drones flying faster than 100mph, referring to Starshield, the military version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite internet network. “The president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the US economy,” Rubio said, noting that the economic restrictions involved a number of countries, not just Russia. Pointing to high energy prices and the Iran war, “we need that period of time to sort of study all this and figure out what the right combination is,” he said. Trump’s abrupt decision to waive sanctions on Russia days before they were to take effect drew outrage Saturday from members of Congress , which had overwhelmingly passed the legislation. Republican Senator Rick Scott said it was clear Russia was the aggressor, and said the US had “to do everything we can to put economic pressure on Russia”. On social media, fellow Republican Thom Tillis described the move as “beyond irresponsible” and a capitulation “to a Russian dictator who illegally invaded Ukraine”. The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy expects the Trump administration to lift more sanctions against Russia in the future and has called for Europe to establish its own negotiations with Moscow as the US has sought better ties and business deals with the Kremlin. “Unfortunately, the lifting of sanctions will continue, and I believe that the ‘diesel deal’ is the first step,” said Zelenskyy on Saturday. “Unfortunately, it seems to me that this cannot stop Putin; on the contrary, he feels joy and happiness that he has such support.” Zelenskyy said Ukraine’s lead negotiator, Rustem Umerov, had met Friday with US presidential envoy Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law . Zelenskyy said the US was working to arrange a three-way meeting involving him, Trump and Putin, potentially in the Middle East, Europe or the US. Russian air defence ⁠units intercepted and destroyed nearly ⁠200 Ukrainian ⁠drones ​headed for Moscow on Saturday, ⁠Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said on Telegram. Sobyanin, ⁠in a long ​series ‌of ‌online posts, noted ‌that 195 drones had been destroyed since midnight, with emergency crews examining debris on ‌the ground. Russia’s civil aviation authority, ​Rosaviatsia, said two Moscow airports – Domodedovo and Vnukovo – had ⁠suspended flight operations. Romania said Saturday it shot down two Russian drones over the Black Sea, the latest in a spate of incidents believed to be spillover from Russia’s invasion of Ukraine . Ships have been attacked in recent days by drones in the Black Sea off the coast of Romania and Bulgaria. Continue reading...

data.title: De local de tiro a santuário, arquipélago de Alcatrazes (SP) renasce dez anos após decreto
data.description: Em vez do barulho dos tiros, há o tamborilar de fragatas macho, com seus papos vermelhos inchados como balões prestes a estourar. Do outro lado de uma das ilhas de Alcatrazes, no meio da mata, o silêncio. Dez anos após um decreto, assinado em 2 de agosto de 2016, ter transformado uma área da Marinha em refúgio de vida silvestre, a recuperação ambiental do arquipélago, no litoral norte paulista , pode ser vista -e ouvida- por todos os lados. data.title: O voto que a economia já não explica
data.description: O governo Lula 3 chega às eleições de 2026 com resultados econômicos que poderiam representar um trunfo eleitoral . A inflação permaneceu relativamente controlada, o desemprego atingiu níveis historicamente baixos, a renda real do trabalho avançou e a pobreza recuou. Ainda assim, o presidente terminou o primeiro turno atrás de Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ). Esse fenômeno não é exclusivamente brasileiro. Na América Latina , eleições recentes mostram que resultados econômicos favoráveis não garantem continuidade política. No Uruguai , em 2024, o governista Álvaro Delgado foi derrotado por Yamandú Orsi , apesar da desaceleração da inflação e da recuperação dos salários reais. No Chile , em 2025, José Antonio Kast venceu Jeannette Jara , candidata apoiada pelo governo de Gabriel Boric , apesar dos avanços no controle da inflação e da retomada do crescimento. Leia mais (10/17/2026 - 22h00)

data.title: Pesquisa da Unesp revela prejuízo auditivo em crianças com microcefalia afetadas pelo zika
data.description: Nos anos de 2015 e 2016, cerca de 1.600 crianças nasceram com a chamada síndrome congênita do zika (SCZ), segundo dados do Ministério da Saúde . Essa condição abrange um conjunto de alterações no feto, provocadas pela infecção da mãe pelo vírus zika durante a gestação. Uma destas alterações é a microcefalia , condição na qual o bebê apresenta a medida da cabeça menor do que a esperada para a idade e o sexo. Mesmo após o pico da crise, os efeitos da infecção continuam a ser investigados. Leia mais (10/17/2026 - 18h00)

data.title: A maldição do vencedor
data.description: Especialmente em momentos de polarização afetiva, esperamos o pior de nossos semelhantes. Tentando ver o lado menos lúgubre das coisas, acho que dá para afirmar que humanos não somos tão maus quanto hoje pode parecer. Como espécie, somos cooperativos. Nosso impulso inicial é o de colaborar com o próximo, mas também não somos trouxas. Deixamos de cooperar a partir do instante que o próximo dá sinais de que não é um parceiro confiável. Faz sentido que seja assim. Se fôssemos seres totalmente egoístas e perfeitamente racionais, sempre empenhados em maximizar ganhos, não teríamos ido muito além do Pleistoceno. Leia mais (10/17/2026 - 14h00)

The conflict in Yemen has entered a dangerous new phase after Iran-backed Houthi rebels targeted the headquarters of Saudi oil giant Aramco in Dhahran.

data.title: DN Debatt. ”Barnen betalar det högsta priset när föräldrarna strider”

data.title: Nya avfallskraven: ”Kommer inte hinnas med”

data.title: De følte, at noget var helt galt på højskoleopholdet, og så optog de mødet i skjul
data.description: En række udenlandske frivillige er de seneste måneder hoppet fra et kursusforløb på Den Rejsende Højskole Lindersvold, der har tilknytning til Tvind. De troede, at de udelukkende skulle arbejde med udviklingsprojekter i Afrika eller Indien. Nu står de frem og fortæller, at de også blev præsenteret for Tvinds særlige ideologi med det mål at rekruttere dem til bevægelsen. Deres historie vidner om, at Tvinds oprindelige ideer fra 1970’erne lever i bedste velgående. Lindersvold erkender udfordringer, men forsvarer højskolens grundide. Fortællingen begynder på et tidligere gods tæt ved Præstø Fjord.

data.title: Masz czerwone kropki na skórze? Tych objawów nie wolno lekceważyć
data.description: Drobne czerwone plamki widoczne na brzuchu i ramionach mogą mieć różne przyczyny. Niekiedy są to łagodne zmiany naczyniowe, innym razem reakcja skóry na kosmetyk lub lek. Jeśli zauważymy takie kropki na ciele, należy obserwować, czy ich wygląd ewoluuje w czasie oraz czy towarzyszą nam inne dolegliwości. Niektóre objawy wymagają pilnej pomocy medycznej.

data.title: Obiekt z czasów Jezusa tkwił w ziemi 2 tys. lat. Wydobyli go w idealnym stanie
data.description: Archeolodzy odnaleźli w Izraelu żydowską łaźnię rytualną pochodzącą z okresu Drugiej Świątyni. Konstrukcja liczy około 2 tys. lat i zachowała się w niemal nienaruszonym stanie. Obiekt waży około 25 ton i trzeba było przenieść go za pomocą dźwigu, aby zabezpieczyć przed uszkodzeniem, ponieważ w okolicy są prowadzone prace budowlane.

data.title: Rusko čelilo jednomu z největších útoků. Ukrajinci udeřili na Petrohrad i Moskvu
data.description: Ruská protivzdušná obrana v noci na neděli zneškodnila 1015 ukrajinských dronů nad 15 ruskými regiony, poloostrovem Krym a Černým mořem, uvedlo ráno ministerstvo obrany v Moskvě. Podle údajů ruské armády jde o jeden z nejrozsáhlejších nočních útoků od zahájení ruské války proti Ukrajině. Ukrajinci podle ruských činitelů mířili na Petrohrad, předtím zasáhli i Moskvu. Ukrajina hlásí ruské útoky, které zabily ženu v Záporoží.

data.title: Stále víc elektromobilů brázdí středočeské silnice. Přibude i bezemisních autobusů
data.description: Když se mluví o elektromobilitě v Česku, je pozornost směřována zejména na Prahu. V závěsu za metropolí je Středočeský kraj. Důvodem je rozvinutá dálniční síť, která ho protíná, i desetitisíce Středočechů, kteří do Prahy denně dojíždějí za prací. V kraji proto přibývá čistě elektrických vozů nejrychlejším tempem v republice.

data.title: Rabování, zpustošená historická radnice. Ve Francii při protestech zadrželi 1 200 lidí
data.description: Násilnosti, které v sobotu provázely v některých francouzských městech celostátní demonstrace, si vyžádaly 150 zraněných policistů a četníků, 1 200 lidí bylo zadrženo. Oznámil to francouzský premiér Sébastien Lecornu. V Paříži bylo zadrženo rekordních 855 lidí, sdělila policie. V sobotu se v celé Francii konaly demonstrace proti zvyšování životních nákladů.

data.title: V říjnu 1896 zažila Praha první promítání, dávali „pradlenu“. Rychlost filmu kolísala
data.description: Když se 18. října 1896 Pražané tísnili v přízemní místnosti hotelu U Černého koně Na Příkopě, uprostřed které jim navíc překážel sloup, neseděli v kinosále, jak ho známe dnes. data.title: Amerika má zpoždění. Proč se tam rychlovlaky na rozdíl od Asie neprosadily
data.description: Z Las Vegas do jižní Kalifornie za pouhé dvě hodiny. Takový je plán americké společnosti Brightline, která připravuje výstavbu přibližně 350 kilometrů dlouhé vysokorychlostní tratě. Vlaky by na ní měly dosahovat rychlosti až 320 kilometrů za hodinu. Přestože jsou podobná spojení hlavně v Asii běžná, Spojené státy v tomto segmentu za světem až do této doby výrazně zaostávaly.

data.title: Skáču do rozjetého vlaku, ve kterém jsem ještě nebyl. Senátor Řehka o svých cílech
data.description: Nově zvolený senátor za obvod Plzeň-město Karel Řehka slavil vítězství společně s manželkou Michaelou v restauraci v centru Plzně. Soupeřku Lucii Kantorovou z ANO porazil nominant STAN ve druhém kole rozdílem bezmála 20 procent hlasů. „Jsem neskutečně vděčný za důvěru, kterou mi voliči dali,“ byla jeho první slova po sečtení hlasů ze všech volebních okrsků.

data.title: Hrozny lepí ruce, slunce pálí. Jak se sklízí na nejvýše položené vinici v Mikulově
data.description: Je odsud dechberoucí výhled do okolí. Přes vinohrad pod známým vrcholem Turold na okraji Mikulova na Břeclavsku by se dalo na krajinu pod sebou dívat i hodiny, zvlášť když zrovna slunce příjemně hřeje a žene venkovní teplotu nahoru. Ale proto tu tentokrát nejsme. Je začátek října a na nejvýše položené mikulovské vinici vrcholí sběr hroznů, které patří pod místní Vinařství Fučík.

data.title: Litva se obávala dronu, vyhlásila červený poplach. Vzlétly stíhačky NATO
data.description: Litvav neděli ráno vyhlásila ve středních a severních regionech země červený stupeň leteckého poplachu a jejich obyvatele vyzvala, aby se odebrali do úkrytů. Příčinou byl neznámý letící objekt, oznámila armáda a národní krizové centrum, uvedla agentura Reuters. Zhruba po hodině armáda poplach odvolala.

data.title: Vojenskou základnu v Kanadě zachvátil požár. Úřady hlásí mrtvé i raněné
data.description: Incident na vojenské základně v kanadské provincii Alberta si vyžádal mrtvé a raněné a způsobil rozsáhlý požár. Oznámil to v sobotu kanadský ministr obrany David McGuinty, aniž by upřesnil, co přesně se stalo.

data.title: Méně žen, vyšší průměrný věk a Grolichův rekord. Zajímavosti o nových senátorech
data.description: Jediná zvolená žena, rekordní počet hlasů pro Jana Grolicha a postup do druhého kola o jediný hlas. Senátní volby 2026 přinesly několik historických výsledků. V horní komoře ubude senátorek a průměrný věk jejích členů vzroste na 58,3 roku.

data.title: Babišovo prvenství. Vládní koalice poprvé v historii nezískala v Senátu ani křeslo
data.description: Vládní strany letos nezískaly ani jedno z 27 senátorských křesel, o která se ve volbách rozhodovalo. Hnutí ANO přitom vyslalo do druhého kola třináct kandidátů, všichni ale prohráli. SPD se do finále nedostalo a Motoristé sobě vlastního kandidáta do Senátu nepostavili. Za třicet let existence Senátu je to poprvé, kdy strany vládní koalice vyšly ze senátních voleb úplně naprázdno.

data.title: Do padelu investoři vložili miliardy. V Británii už ale první firmy krachují
data.description: Padel zažívá nejen ve Velké Británii nebývalý rozmach. Do výstavby nových hřišť investoři ve Spojeném království vložili stovky milionů dolarů a další sportovní centra rychle přibývají. S rostoucí konkurencí se však objevují první problémy. Někteří provozovatelé už zkrachovali a další se obávají, že se jim vložené peníze nevrátí.

data.title: Přes všechny úspěchy grant nedostanu. To se mi uzavřelo. David Ondříček vypráví
data.description: Po letech se vrací k poetice filmů Šeptej a Samotáři. Režisér, scenárista a producent David Ondříček přichází se svým osmým celovečerním filmem. Snímek Kluci to vidí jinak než holky, jehož premiéra v kinech spadá na 22. října, má ambici navázat na kultovní Samotáře – a znovu se s humorem, jemnou ironií i trochou drsnosti podívat na život třicátníků až padesátníků.

data.title: Bosse s manželkou vyfotil na pláži. Za drzou reportáž dostal dvě kulky do hlavy
data.description: Nikdo nesměl vědět, jak vypadá, chtěl jen ze zákulisí tahat za nitky. Přesto tvář Alfreda Yabrána uviděla celá Argentina. A jako by to nestačilo, reportéři ho vyfotili na dovolené. V trenclích! Tragický příběh protřelého kmotra a novináře, který jeho totožnost odhalil, přináší další díl seriálu Slavné fotografie.

data.title: Pohled na lidi s pečivem v sáčku je ničil. Vyrobili alternativu k plastovým pytlíkům
data.description: Strkáte v obchodě pečivo do mikrotenových sáčků? Analýza ukázala, že průměrná doba jejich životnosti je pouhých 6 minut. Řada z nás se totiž na pečivo hladově vrhne hned za kasou. Mikrotenový sáček pak vyhodí přímo v obchodě, nebo až později doma, často putuje jen do směsného odpadu. Dva nadšenci z Česka se snaží udělat neekologickému plýtvání přítrž, píše magazín Víkend DNES.

data.title: Pohlaďte ho v rozkroku, přináší to štěstí. Vítejte na ostrově, kde je Ronaldo bohem
data.description: Vlahý říjnový den, kdy z prudkých svahů nad Funchalem, metropolí portugalského souostroví Madeira, vzlíná vlhký opar z prudkého odpoledního lijáku, na fotbalovém plácku už se prohánějí malí kluci. Jeden jako druhý má na zádech číslo 7. Jak jinak. Mají ikonické číslo, které si pro sebe vyhradil slavný zdejší rodák, hvězdný Cristiano Ronaldo. Zkráceně CR7. Celým jménem Cristiano Ronaldo dos Santos Aveiro. Každý tu chce být jako on.

data.title: Po třech letech tlaku z Číny úspěch. Písecká textilka našla recept na Temu
data.description: Josef Handrejch se pustil do podnikání spolu s manželkou Lenou v roce 2011. Začali vyrábět povlečení, prostěradla a další bytový textil z evropských materiálů. Jejich písecká textilka Kvalitex rostla postupně a dařilo se jim i v době covidu. Na kolena je srazil masivní nástup asijského tržiště Temu na český trh. Odmítli ale zničující cenovou válku a zvolili jinou strategii. Riskantní změna se vyplatila.

data.title: Nic nezákonného jsem nedělala. Favoritka z ANO Brzyszkowská o tom, proč prohrála
data.description: Byla největší nadějí hnutí ANO v letošních senátních volbách. Ale Lenka Brzyszkowská, starostka Orlové, pozici favoritky nepotvrdila a v Karviné překvapivě prohrála s Petrem Kazíkem. data.title: Francie vře. Do ulic vyšly statisíce lidí, policejní granát utrhl demonstrantovi ruku
data.description: Proti vysokým životním nákladům v sobotu ve Francii protestovaly statisíce lidí. Podle organizátorů jich do ulic vyšlo až 800 tisíc, ministerstvo vnitra uvádí 550 tisíc. Demonstrace v Paříži i dalších městech provázely střety s policií, rabování a útoky na úřady. Ve městě Saint-Étienne přišel jeden z demonstrantů po zásahu policejním granátem o ruku.

data.title: Rumuni sestřelili nad Černým mořem dva drony. Narušily vzdušný prostor země
data.description: Dvě rumunské stíhačky F-16 v sobotu nad výsostnými vodami země v Černém moři sestřelily dva bezpilotní letouny. Podle tamního ministerstva obrany šlo o útočné drony typu Geraň, ruskou variantu íránských Šáhedů. Oba stroje byly zneškodněny krátce po sobě.

data.title: Protesty nejen ve Francii. Do ulic vyšli lidé v Portugalsku, Itálii i Belgii
data.description: Protesty proti ekonomické a sociální situaci se v sobotu kromě Francie konaly také v Portugalsku, Itálii a Belgii. V Lisabonu vyšly do ulic desítky tisíc lidí kvůli rostoucím nákladům na bydlení a život. V Bruselu a Lutychu stovky lidí protestovaly proti změnám ve školství a policejním zásahům. V Itálii demonstrovali odboráři i mladí lidé.

data.title: Výsledek voleb je katastrofální. Hnutí ANO čeká restart, říká Babiš
data.description: Vládní hnutí ANO mělo ve druhém kole senátních voleb nejvíce kandidátů, celkem 13. Nepodařilo se mu však zvítězit v jediném obvodě. V letošních volbách hnutí premiéra Andreje Babiše obhajovalo jednu pozici, v Senátu si tak dokonce pohoršilo. „Pro naše hnutí je výsledek katastrofální. Jak v komunálních, tak senátních volbách,“ zhodnotil předseda vlády.

data.title: Voliči oceňují a chtějí spolupráci stran, říká Němcová. Líbila by se jí čtyřkoalice
data.description: Výsledky senátních voleb podle Miroslavy Němcové z ODS ukázaly, že voliči oceňují spolupráci stran a chtějí ji. Němcová, která v horní komoře končí a odchází i z vrcholné politiky, by podpořila volební spojení stran původní koalice SPOLU s hnutím STAN do čtyřkoalice. „Mně by se to líbilo. Určitě bych s tím neměla žádný problém,“ prohlásila v rozhovoru pro iDNES.cz.

Němcová, která v horní komoře končí a odchází i z vrcholné politiky, by podpořila volební spojení stran původní koalice SPOLU s hnutím STAN do čtyřkoalice. „Mně by se to líbilo. Určitě bych s tím neměla žádný problém,“ prohlásila v rozhovoru pro iDNES.cz.

data.title: Nejvíc voličů za 15 let. Volební účast v 2. kole byla rekordní
data.description: Letošní účast ve druhém kole senátních voleb je nejvyšší od roku 2010, přišlo 21,12 procenta voličů. Je to téměř o 4,5 procentního bodu více než před šesti lety, kdy v obvodech, kde se volilo i letos, volilo 16,73 procenta lidí. Rekordní účast byla 32,55 procenta v roce 2002.

data.title: ANALÝZA: Proč Rakušan slaví. Volby byly hlavně o symbolických vzkazech
data.description: Po zveřejnění výsledků komunálních a prvního kola senátních voleb šéf hnutí ANO Andrej Babiš s místopředsedou Karlem Havlíčkem vykládali, že to sice nebylo tak dobré, jak čekali, ale úplně špatné také ne. Když se sečetly hlasy po druhém kole senátního klání, už to premiér a předseda ANO řekl natvrdo: „Pro naše hnutí je výsledek katastrofální. Jak v komunálních, tak senátních volbách.“

data.title: OBRAZEM: Zklamaný Babiš, slavící Řehka s půllitrem i Láska na cestě za soupeřem
data.description: Druhé kolo senátních voleb rozhodlo o podobě horní komory na další dva roky. Starostové slavili, šéf hnutí ANO Andrej Babiš označil výsledek svého hnutí za katastrofální. data.title: RDC : près de 900 enfants nés avec un pied bot pris en charge gratuitement en 9 mois
data.description: Près de 900 enfants nés avec un pied bot ont bénéficié d’une prise en charge gratuite en République démocratique du Congo (RDC) entre janvier et septembre 2026. Le pied bot est une malformation congénitale qui entraîne une déformation du pied, lequel est tourné vers l’intérieur ou vers le bas.

data.title: Coupe du monde U15 : Zico Tumba sélectionne 14 Léopards pour représenter la RDC
data.description: Le sélectionneur national des Léopards U15, Zico Tumba, a dévoilé, ce samedi 17 octobre 2026, la liste des 14 joueurs retenus pour la première édition de la Coupe du monde U15 et Festival de la FIFA. La liste a été rendue publique lors d’une conférence de presse organisée à la salle de presse du stade des Martyrs, à Kinshasa. La compétition se déroulera en Azerbaïdjan, du 22 au 31 octobre 2026. La RDC évoluera dans le groupe D, aux côtés du Salvador, de la Tunisie, du Brésil, de la Guinée-Bissau et du Népal.

data.title: Ligue des champions de la CAF : le TP Mazembe accroché par le Club Africain (1-1)
data.description: Le TP Mazembe et le Club Africain de Tunis se sont neutralisés (1-1), ce samedi 17 octobre 2026, au stade TP Mazembe de Lubumbashi dans le Haut-Katanga, en match aller du deuxième tour préliminaire de la Ligue des champions de la CAF. Les Corbeaux ont manqué l’occasion de prendre l’avantage avant le match retour, après l’annulation d’un but à la 89e minute. Le TP Mazembe a ouvert le score à la 38e minute grâce à Josué Kazema. Mais l’avantage des Congolais n’a duré qu’une minute : à la 39e, Alain Kanté a égalisé pour le Club Africain.

data.title: RDC : les écogardes de l’Upemba récompensés aux African Conservation Awards 2026
data.description: Les écogardes du parc national de l’Upemba, dans la province du Haut-Katanga, ont remporté le prix « Best Ranger Team », qui récompense la meilleure équipe d’écogardes, aux African Conservation Awards 2026. data.title: 300 ex-combattants et déplacés bénéficient de projets de réinsertion socio-économique en Ituri
data.description: Trois cents ex-combattants et personnes déplacées de guerre bénéficient de projets de réinsertion socio-économique dans plusieurs localités des territoires d’Irumu, de Djugu et de Mahagi, en Ituri. Financées par la MONUSCO et mises en œuvre par l’ONG Femme en action pour le développement multisectoriel (FADEM), ces initiatives combinent formation professionnelle, rémunération des bénéficiaires et construction d’infrastructures de base pour favoriser la paix et la cohésion sociale.

The offerings range from building materials and home appliances to real estate financing options and property development services.

data.title: ‘We voted for a reset, not equalization’ – Senyo Hosi on EC appointments
data.description:
Convenor of the One Ghana Movement and policy analyst Senyo Hosi has described President John Dramani Mahama’s appointment of Emelia Afi Agbenyo as a Deputy Chairperson of the Electoral Commission (EC) as one of his biggest disappointments with the administration.

President Mahama appointed Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah and Emelia Afi Agbenyo as Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission.

Ms Agbenyo previously served as an NDC manifesto spokesperson and as Director of Legal Affairs for the party’s Women’s Wing. Her appointment has drawn criticism from the New Patriotic Party (NPP), which has called for it to be withdrawn.

data.title: Parliament must not be a spectator in BRICS decision – Hassan Ayariga
data.description:
The Founder and Leader of the All People’s Congress (APC), Hassan Ayariga, has called on Parliament to scrutinise the government’s proposed move to join BRICS, warning against excluding elected representatives from major national decisions.

In a press statement issued on Saturday, October 17, 2026, Dr Ayariga urged the Speaker of Parliament, the Majority and Minority leadership, and all Members of Parliament to demand a comprehensive briefing from the Minister for Foreign Affairs on the proposed partnership.

“Parliament must demand a comprehensive briefing from the Minister for Foreign Affairs concerning the proposed BRICS partnership,” he stated.

data.title: Ghana must protect national interest in pursuit of BRICS membership – Hassan Ayariga
data.description:
The Founder and Leader of the All People’s Congress (APC), Hassan Ayariga, has cautioned Ghana against exchanging one form of economic dependency for another as the government pursues membership of the BRICS economic bloc.

In a press statement issued on Saturday, October 17, 2026, Ayariga said he was not opposed to Ghana establishing strategic relationships with BRICS countries but insisted that such partnerships must protect the country’s national interests, constitutional governance and democratic accountability.

He argued that any move to join the bloc must deliver tangible benefits for Ghanaian citizens and businesses rather than create new forms of economic dependence.

data.title: Hassan Ayariga challenges Mahama over BRICS move, demands parliamentary consultation
data.description:
The Founder and Leader of the All People’s Congress (APC), Dr Hassan Ayariga, has challenged President John Dramani Mahama over the government’s plan to pursue Ghana’s membership of BRICS, demanding parliamentary scrutiny and public consultation on the decision.

In a statement issued on Saturday, October 17, 2026, Dr Ayariga questioned whether Cabinet could determine Ghana’s long-term international economic and geopolitical commitments without broader public and parliamentary engagement.

“Who gave Cabinet the authority to decide for over 34 million Ghanaians without parliamentary and public consultation?” he asked.

data.title: Belgium-based ICGC pastor enstooled Amanonehene of Abotakyi
data.description:
A 44-year-old Reverend Minister of the International Central Gospel Church (ICGC), Rev. Richard Tagoe, has been enstooled Amanonehene of Abotakyi in the Akuapem Traditional Area of the Eastern Region, with a pledge to mobilise diaspora support and attract investment for the town’s development.

The businessman, who lives in Belgium, assumes the traditional title Nana Ohene Tagoe I.

The Amanonehene title is intended to promote the welfare of indigenes living abroad and mobilise their support for development projects in the town.

Following the traditional rites, Nana Ohene Tagoe I was carried shoulder-high and paraded through the principal streets of Abotakyi amid cheers, drumming and dancing.

data.title: BLR Boys push the boundaries of Afrobeats and Hip-Hop with new single ‘Lapdance’ featuring 6uff
data.description:
The Ghanaian group joins forces with Nigerian rising star 6uff on an Afrofusion and Dancehall record celebrating ambition, chemistry, and the rewards of the hustle. Emerging as one of the most compelling group movements of 2026, the BLR Boys continue to push the boundaries of contemporary African music with the release of their new single, ‘Lapdance,’ featuring Nigerian rising star 6uff.

Blending Afrofusion, Dancehall, Afrobeats, and Hip-Hop influences, the record captures the group's evolving sound while reinforcing the brotherhood and trust at the centre of their identity. Built on a foundation of street support and shared ambition, the BLR Boys represent a generation of young African creatives determined to turn everyday struggles into something bigger. Their story reflects the experiences of local hustlers, young dreamers, and communities navigating the daily pressures of life while holding on to the promise of a better future.

data.title: Électricité à Antananarivo : de nouvelles coupures dès ce vendredi 16 octobre, sur fond de déficit de 18 MW
data.description: Les habitants d'Antananarivo subissent une nouvelle vague de délestages. Depuis plusieurs jours, de nombreux quartiers de la capitale connaissent des interruptions d'électricité, parfois plus longues que les horaires annoncés par la Jirama. Cette situation intervient alors que la compagnie nationale prévoit également des travaux d'entretien du réseau du 16 au 22 octobre. À l'origine de ces perturbations figure l'indisponibilité de la centrale thermique TAC 1 d'Ambohimanambola. (…) - Energie

data.title: Asociación Hermanos Saiz: cuatro décadas de vanguardia y compromiso con el arte joven cubano.
data.description: La Asociación Hermanos Saiz (AHS), celebra este 18 de octubre sus 40 años de fundación, consolidada como la organización que aglutina la vanguardia artística e intelectual de Cuba. En sus 40 años, la organización ha demostrado que el arte joven cubano no solo resiste, sino que se reinventa, desde el ejemplo de dos adolescentes que dieron su vida por sus ideales. The post Asociación Hermanos Saiz: cuatro décadas de vanguardia y compromiso con el arte joven cubano. first appeared on Cubadebate .

data.description: Una empresa intentó cobrar un incumplimiento contractual a otra compañía mediante un arbitraje, pero no lo logró pese a que el contrato entre las dos partes contemplaba esa vía. data.title: Tiktoker Rambito hace historia con gol en el fútbol de Honduras
data.description: El fútbol hondureño dejó una de esas imágenes que rápidamente se roban las miradas en las redes sociales. Dixon Alvarado , conocido popularmente como “Rambito” , el tiktoker de baja estatura, se convirtió en protagonista de la penúltima jornada del torneo Apertura de la Liga de Ascenso al marcar uno de los goles del triunfo del Brasilia frente al Juventud Yoreña. El popular creador de contenido ingresó al terreno de juego y no tardó en demostrar que también quería dejar su huella con el balón. En medio de un partido cargado de emociones, Rambito aprovechó su oportunidad para sumarse a la fiesta goleadora del conjunto brasileño, que consiguió una anotación que desató la alegría de sus compañeros y aficionados. La jugada del quinto tanto llegó después de un gran contragolpe del Brasilia . La acción terminó con Dixon Alvarado enviando el balón al fondo de la red para establecer el quinto gol de su equipo y sentenciar el marcador ante el Juventud Yoreña, en un momento que parecía sacado de una historia de película. La celebración fue especial: apenas el balón cruzó la línea de gol, sus compañeros corrieron a abrazarlo para festejar con él la anotación. Rambito recibió el cariño del grupo en una escena que reflejó la emoción por su participación y que rápidamente llamó la atención de quienes siguen las incidencias del fútbol de ascenso hondureño. Así, Dixon Alvarado, conocido como Rambito 0.5 o Rambito del Paraíso en las redes sociales, vivió un momento inolvidable con el Brasilia.

data.title: Nicolás Ochoa rechaza informe por presunto desfalco de L7 millones y denuncia “arbitrariedades”
data.description: S an Pedro Sula, Honduras.- Nicolás Ochoa, exdirector del Centro Técnico Hondureño Alemán (CTHA) rompió el silencio frente a la investigación que señala presuntas anomalías por más de siete millones de lempiras en el manejo de recursos de un centro educativo técnico de San Pedro Sula. El exdirector rechazó la veracidad del informe divulgado por las autoridades educativas y denunció que se ha dañado su dignidad personal y profesional antes de que se esclarezcan los hechos. En una declaración pública dirigida a padres de familia, estudiantes, docentes y ciudadanía en general, Ochoa cuestionó al director departamental de Educación de Cortés, Rafael Eduardo Rodríguez Bonilla, por divulgar información sobre la investigación sin que, según afirmó, se le haya comunicado oficialmente el contenido del informe. “Usted ha hecho público un informe que desconozco, que no se me ha hecho la comunicación oficial en ningún momento”, manifestó Ochoa, quien pidió que se respeten los procedimientos administrativos y su derecho a defenderse antes de que se establezca alguna responsabilidad. El exdirector del CTHA también puso en duda que existan faltantes de documentos de respaldo por alrededor de siete millones de lempiras. Explicó que estuvo a cargo de la administración de los fondos aportados por los padres de familia entre 2023 y 2025, mientras que en los años anteriores, según su versión, esos recursos eran manejados por las sociedades de padres de familia mediante una cuenta bancaria distinta. Ochoa argumentó que las aportaciones de los padres son voluntarias y que no todas las familias realizan esos pagos. Por esa razón, consideró que el monto señalado en el informe no corresponde con los recursos que, según él, se recaudaron durante el período bajo su administración. La postura de Ochoa contrasta con los resultados divulgados por la Dirección Departamental de Educación de Cortés. Rafael Rodríguez, confirmó que una comisión técnica de la Secretaría de Educación, después de más de cinco meses de intervención, encontró deficiencias en la administración financiera, así como en los procesos administrativos, técnico-pedagógicos y curriculares del instituto. “En la parte de administración financiera, en la utilización de los fondos propios, tenemos un hallazgo del cual hace falta un poquito más de siete millones de lempiras”, manifestó Rodríguez al explicar los resultados de la revisión. El funcionario indicó que el centro educativo manejaba ingresos anuales que oscilaban entre 10 y 15 millones de lempiras y que se identificaron retrasos en los procesos de liquidación de los fondos propios. También señaló que durante seis años no se realizaron las declaraciones correspondientes, según los hallazgos expuestos sobre la gestión financiera. Ante los resultados, Rodríguez anunció que la Dirección Departamental iniciará las actuaciones legales recomendadas en el informe y que notificará formalmente a Ochoa sobre los hallazgos. Hasta el momento, no se ha informado de una resolución definitiva que establezca responsabilidades individuales por los recursos observados. Por su parte, Ana Colindres, abogada que encabezó la comisión interventora, indicó que la revisión encontró problemas en distintos procedimientos de la institución. “Más que irregularidades, encontramos vicios o falta de conocimiento de los procedimientos. Un director no puede alegar desconocimiento de la ley ni de los reglamentos que regulan su función”, expresó. Uno de los señalamientos más delicados de Ochoa está relacionado con la documentación que habría sido utilizada durante las investigaciones. Aseguró que los comprobantes, facturas, cheques, recibos y movimientos bancarios fueron trasladados en cinco cajas selladas a la Dirección Departamental de Educación. Según su relato, las cajas permanecieron más de diez días en esas instalaciones y posteriormente fueron devueltas poco a poco y abiertas. Ochoa sostuvo que esta situación genera dudas sobre la veracidad del informe, aunque no presentó en su declaración pública pruebas que permitan corroborar de manera independiente lo denunciado. El exdirector defendió además su trayectoria de aproximadamente 40 años al frente del centro educativo y aseguró que su gestión contribuyó a formar jóvenes con competencias laborales para desempeñarse en Honduras y otros países. Ochoa también cuestionó la decisión de trasladarlo a una dirección distrital en calidad de asistente, medida que calificó como una reducción de categoría adoptada sin que, según él, se haya demostrado su culpabilidad. “Por lo tanto, no siga cometiendo arbitrariedades y poniendo mi dignidad en los medios y humillándome públicamente”, expresó al dirigirse al director departamental de Educación. Finalmente, pidió a los medios de comunicación que también den espacio a su versión para que la ciudadanía conozca las distintas posiciones sobre el caso. Hasta que se conozca el informe íntegro y se aclaren los señalamientos, las presuntas irregularidades en el manejo de los recursos deben mantenerse como objeto de investigación y no como responsabilidades demostradas.

data.title: Messi firma dos golazos 'maradonianos' en la MLS y se acerca a Cristiano Ronaldo
data.description: En su regreso al Mercedes-Benz Stadium de Atlanta, donde este verano dio una asistencia clave en la victoria de Argentina contra Inglaterra en las semifinales del Mundial de Norteamérica, Lionel Messi dio un nuevo recital y refrendó la victoria del Inter Miami por 3-1 contra el Atlanta United con un espectacular doblete. Messi alcanzó los 25 goles en la MLS para reforzar su condición de máximo artillero de la liga estadounidense esta temporada y entregó a las Garzas del técnico Cristian González el tercer triunfo consecutivo, esta vez en un duelo de preparadores argentinos con Gerardo 'Tata' Martin o . Fue Germán Berterame quien inauguró el marcador con un cabezazo al borde del descanso tras un centro del uruguayo Luis Suárez.Hubo tiempo en el 51 para un milagro del meta del Inter Miami , Dayne St. Clair, ante el paraguayo Miguel Almirón, antes de que Messi comenzara su festival anotador. Leo anotó el 2-0 en una espectacular jugada personal en la que arrancó desde la línea del centro del campo, combinó con Berterame y llegó a regatear hasta a su propio compañero antes de definir con la zurda. Era el 56 y cuatro minutos después completó su doblete personal con una jugada parecida, con un 'eslalon' entre rivales en el área de penalti antes de fulminar al meta. DATOS DE SOFASCORE SOBRE EL ATLANTA VS INTER MIAMI En el minuto 89, el ex del Inter Miami Fafa Picaul t anotó el gol del honor para el Atlanta desde el punto de penalti. El Inter Miami es segundo en el Este, con 55 puntos, a once de un Nashville que domina la tabla. Cristiano Ronaldo continúa liderando cómodamente el ranking histórico de goleadores, con 981 goles en 1.335 partidos disputados. Lionel Messi sigue siendo su perseguidor más cercano. El argentino acumula 936 goles oficiales en 1.180 partidos y mantiene viva una rivalidad que marcó una era en el fútbol mundial. Actualmente, la diferencia entre ambos es de 45 goles. Aunque el margen todavía es amplio, tanto Cristiano como Messi continúan activos y sosteniendo números impresionantes incluso en la recta final de sus carreras.

data.title: “El Teniente” llega a juzgados por el secuestro y crimen del hijo del expresidente Ricardo Maduro
data.description: San Pedro Sula, Honduras. – Casi tres décadas después del secuestro y asesinato de Ricardo Ernesto Maduro Andrews , hijo del expresidente hondureño Ricardo Maduro, un sospechoso vinculado al caso fue remitido este sábado al Centro Integrado de Justicia Penal (CEIN) de San Pedro Sula. Se trata de Marco Antonio Ávila Castellanos , quien fue puesto a disposición de la Secretaría Adjunta del Juzgado de Letras de lo Penal de la Sección Judicial de San Pedro Sula por agentes de la Dirección Policial de Investigaciones (DPI). De acuerdo con la información proporcionada, contra Ávila Castellanos existía una orden de captura emitida el 1 de junio de 2004, por su presunta vinculación con el secuestro y asesinato de Maduro Andrews, ocurrido el 23 de abril de 1997. Según la agenda judicial, el sospechoso comparecerá durante este sábado ante las autoridades para la audiencia indagatoria, conforme al procedimiento penal aplicable al caso. El expediente se remonta a uno de los crímenes que conmocionaron a Honduras en la década de 1990, por involucrar al hijo de quien posteriormente llegó a ocupar la Presidencia de la República. La comparecencia ante el juzgado permitirá avanzar en las diligencias judiciales relacionadas con el caso, mientras las autoridades competentes deberán determinar la situación jurídica del sospechoso conforme a la ley.

data.title: Tabla de posiciones: Motagua alza vuelvo y se acerca al liderato que tiene Olimpia
data.description: El Fútbol Club Motagua alzó vuelo en Puerto Cortés y consiguió una importante victoria de 2-0 frente al Platense, en duelo correspondiente a la jornada 10 del Torneo Apertura 2026 de la Liga Nacional de Honduras. El conjunto capitalino hizo valer su condición de favorito y regresó a casa con tres puntos que le permiten mantenerse en la pelea por los primeros puestos de la clasificación. El Ciclón Azul tuvo que trabajar para conseguir el resultado, pero encontró las respuestas necesarias en la segunda parte, cuando dos jugadores que ingresaron desde el banquillo terminaron marcando la diferencia. Aarón Barrios y Jeffry Miranda fueron los encargados de enviar el balón al fondo de las redes, convirtiéndose en protagonistas de una victoria fundamental para los intereses del vigente campeón del fútbol hondureño. Con este resultado, el equipo dirigido por el español Javier López confirmó su buen momento en el campeonato nacional y encadenó su segunda victoria consecutiva. Motagua comienza a encontrar regularidad en el torneo y demuestra que tiene argumentos para competir por los primeros lugares, en una lucha por el liderato que se mantiene intensa. Los tres puntos conseguidos en territorio porteño tienen un valor importante para las aspiraciones del conjunto azul. Con este triunfo, Motagua llegó a 19 unidades en la tabla de posiciones del Torneo Apertura 2026 , consolidándose en la cuarta posición de la clasificación y ampliando su ventaja sobre los equipos que lo persiguen. Uno de los clubes que queda más rezagado respecto al Ciclón es Olancho FC , que se encuentra en la quinta posición con 12 puntos. Sin embargo, el gran objetivo de Motagua es acercarse al liderato que actualmente pertenece al Olimpia , que suma 23 puntos. Con 19 unidades en su cuenta, los azules se colocan a cuatro del primer lugar y mantienen la presión sobre su máximo rival en la lucha por dominar el campeonato. Más allá de su importancia en la clasificación de la Liga Nacional, la victoria frente al Platense llega en un momento clave para Motagua, que tiene por delante uno de los desafíos más importantes de su calendario. El equipo de Javier López se prepara para enfrentarse a la Liga Deportiva Alajuelense en las semifinales de la Copa Centroamericana , una serie en la que estará en juego el boleto a la gran final del certamen regional. La otra cara de la moneda es la del Platense, que continúa atravesando un complicado momento en el campeonato hondureño. Los escualos no consiguieron aprovechar su condición de local y terminaron cediendo los tres puntos ante un Motagua que supo resolver el encuentro en la segunda parte. Con apenas ocho puntos en la clasificación, el conjunto porteño permanece comprometido en la zona baja de la tabla y necesita reaccionar cuanto antes para evitar que la distancia con sus rivales directos continúe aumentando. Cabe destacar que el Platense-Motagua fue el tercer encuentro disputado en la jornada 10 del Torneo Apertura 2026 de la Liga Nacional de Honduras. Previamente, Marathón derrotó 2-1 al Olancho FC, mientras que Olimpia se impuso por el mismo marcador al Real España.

Sin embargo, el gran objetivo de Motagua es acercarse al liderato que actualmente pertenece al Olimpia , que suma 23 puntos. Con 19 unidades en su cuenta, los azules se colocan a cuatro del primer lugar y mantienen la presión sobre su máximo rival en la lucha por dominar el campeonato. Más allá de su importancia en la clasificación de la Liga Nacional, la victoria frente al Platense llega en un momento clave para Motagua, que tiene por delante uno de los desafíos más importantes de su calendario. El equipo de Javier López se prepara para enfrentarse a la Liga Deportiva Alajuelense en las semifinales de la Copa Centroamericana , una serie en la que estará en juego el boleto a la gran final del certamen regional. La otra cara de la moneda es la del Platense, que continúa atravesando un complicado momento en el campeonato hondureño. Los escualos no consiguieron aprovechar su condición de local y terminaron cediendo los tres puntos ante un Motagua que supo resolver el encuentro en la segunda parte. Con apenas ocho puntos en la clasificación, el conjunto porteño permanece comprometido en la zona baja de la tabla y necesita reaccionar cuanto antes para evitar que la distancia con sus rivales directos continúe aumentando. Cabe destacar que el Platense-Motagua fue el tercer encuentro disputado en la jornada 10 del Torneo Apertura 2026 de la Liga Nacional de Honduras. Previamente, Marathón derrotó 2-1 al Olancho FC, mientras que Olimpia se impuso por el mismo marcador al Real España.
